brief: US equities closed lower in the year's lowest-volume session (Columbus Day); European equities closed higher, led by defensives. Median S&P breadth is at its worst since the dot-com bubble (15% below 52-week highs), while the S&P's one-week implied move was only about 1% into CPI, Fed speakers and earnings this week. Memory-led semi weakness continued on China's domestic progress, Korea's KOSPI follow-through (-365bps), and desk flows turning better-for-sale. Ahead of Wednesday's print, GS forecasts September core CPI +0.24% m/m (above 0.2% consensus, putting y/y at 2.46% vs 2.5% consensus), headline +0.59% on energy, and a slightly smaller 0.20% core PCE. Cross-asset, GS shifts to OW equities/UW credit over 3 months and OW bonds/cash over 12 months on earnings growth and improved valuation asymmetry into Q3, keeping OW US/Asia, UW Europe, and a barbell of tech plus rate-sensitive, high-dividend, low-vol names for eventual rate relief. LVMH's headline sales grew 1% cFX, in line, but Fashion and Leather, its key profit driver, fell 5% cFX, worse than consensus (-2%), GS's estimate (-2.5%) and already-reduced expectations, on a Chinese cluster down mid-teens. GS also initiates CTS Eventim (N), downgrades Orsted (N) on rising sovereign rates, and reinstates Zurich (N).
